{
  "subtype": "faceted_decomposition",
  "concept": "airline_service_quality",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "cabin_crew_service_quality",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "In-flight crew attentiveness/professionalism is a core people-service aspect OF airline service quality — a genuine part-of the concept, not an external predictor. Its ordinal categories (exceptional_attentive → rude_dismissive) directly describe a constituent dimension of the service experience."
    },
    {
      "name": "operational_reliability",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Punctuality/delays/cancellations constitute the 'reliability' dimension of service quality (a recognized SERVQUAL-style facet). It is an aspect OF the experience the traveller receives, not merely a cause or predictor of it, so it qualifies as a constitutive part."
    },
    {
      "name": "seat_comfort_configuration",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Seat/cabin comfort is the tangible-product facet of airline service quality — an aspect OF the concept. (It somewhat mirrors the original 'Seat Comfort' column, but judged against the concept itself it is a legitimate constitutive facet.)"
    },
    {
      "name": "customer_service_responsiveness",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Responsiveness to inquiries/complaints is the 'responsiveness' dimension of service quality, an aspect OF the concept. However it partially overlaps the staff-helpfulness content already captured by cabin crew and ground service (note shared value 'slow_unhelpful'), so it is a facet but not cleanly disjoint."
    },
    {
      "name": "ground_service_quality",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Check-in/boarding/airport handling is the ground-touchpoint facet of the overall service experience — a constitutive part-of the concept, distinct in channel from in-flight crew service."
    }
  ],
  "facet_columns": [
    "cabin_crew_service_quality",
    "operational_reliability",
    "seat_comfort_configuration",
    "customer_service_responsiveness",
    "ground_service_quality"
  ],
  "non_facet_columns": [],
  "mutual_exclusivity": 0.7,
  "exhaustiveness": 0.7,
  "rationale": "All five added columns pass the meronymy test: each is an aspect OF airline_service_quality (people service in the cabin, people service on the ground, customer-service responsiveness, operational reliability, and seat/cabin comfort) rather than an external predictor, cause, or restatement of the whole. Mutual exclusivity is only moderate because three of the facets are people-service dimensions (cabin crew, ground, and customer-service responsiveness) whose 'staff helpfulness/responsiveness' content overlaps — the customer_service_responsiveness facet in particular shares scale content with the crew and ground facets (e.g., the common 'slow_unhelpful' level), so the carve-up is not fully non-overlapping. Exhaustiveness is reasonable but incomplete against the concept: it covers staff service, reliability, and comfort well, yet omits well-recognized constitutive facets such as food & beverage quality, in-flight entertainment, cleanliness, and value-for-money — the decomposition is people/operations/comfort-heavy and leaves several product-experience dimensions uncovered."
}
